title: The railway age
summary: Canals had long been Britain's best way to move goods, but railways offered a cheaper and much faster alternative. On 27 September 1825 the Locomotion, on the opening day of the Stockton and Darlington Railway, carried the first railway passengers in northeast England. In 1829 Robert Stephenson's Rocket followed. This outline covers the British start of the railway age.

uncertainty.note: Begins with the inaugural run of the Stockton and Darlington Railway on 27 September 1825; end is approximate, marking the peak of railway primacy before automobile competition.

where.modern_name: Darlington, England (where the railway age began; later worldwide)
where.historical_name: Darlington, County Durham, United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

importance.justification: The advent of the steam locomotive railway transformed global overland transportation, enabling the industrial revolution, mass long-distance passenger travel, and integrated national and international economies.

sources.title: Steam locomotive No. 1 'Locomotion', Stockton & Darlington Railway

reviewer_note: Trevithick ran earlier steam railway engines from 1803. Railways later spread worldwide, including the records for Japan and the Trans-Siberian, but this outline covers Britain. The end date is approximate.
